# Publications

# Publications

Dee Hock published four books. These are divided into two separate projects.

The first and most famous project is “The Birth of the Chaordic Age (1999)”, which was updated later in a second edition renamed “One from Many (2005)”.

...

The second group of projects is “The Autobiography of a Restless Mind (2013)”, which came in two volumes. It reads like a series of quotes or ‘tweets’ concerning things like the structure of the world, business ideas and ideas of how to live well.

There are details below of each of them alongside links to purchase them if you would wish. They are not affiliate links.

# Birth of the Chaordic Age (1999)

# Autobiography of a Restless Mind (2013)

Autobiography of a Restless Mind is a fascinating, exceptionally diverse collection of observations and reflections written over the past twenty-five years by one of the most innovative thinkers, writers, and leaders of the past half century. Witty and wise, playful and profound, prophetic and immensely quotable, it is a companion no thinking, caring person should be without.

A restless mind, still in print

Hock turned his experience into Birth of the Chaordic Age in 1999. An updated edition appeared as One from Many in 2005. In 2013 came the two-volume Autobiography of a Restless Mind, a different kind of project built around short observations. The titles trace his continuing interests: the emergence of a system, the relationship between individuals and a whole, and a mind reluctant to stop asking questions.

Inspirational Quotes by Dee Hock (American Businessman)

Dee Ward Hock (1920–2022) was an American financial businessman. He was the founder of the global payments company Visa.
Born in North Ogden, Utah, Hock ended his formal schooling after two years at a community college. Appointed in 1966 to run a new credit-card unit at National Bank of Commerce in Seattle, a licensee of BankAmericard, Hock discovered a pattern of consumer fraud, bad debts, and paperwork snarls. He arose as the leader of a committee of executives from 100 bank licensees.

...

Hock served as National BankAmericard 1970–84, helping it grow customer billings dramatically and gaining worldwide name recognition. After an employee contest in 1976, Hock renamed his company Visa Inc. At his death, Visa had 3.9 billion cards in circulation worldwide.
After retirement, Hock became “a ranch owner, recluse, student, and philosopher,” wrote aphorisms, and compiled them in books. His memoirs are One from Many: VISA and the Rise of Chaordic Organization (2005) and Autobiography of a Restless Mind: Reflections on the Human Condition (2012.) His other works include Birth of the Chaordic Age (1999.)
